definitionEn: making you feel trapped and anxious, especially in a small or crowded space
senseNote: Здесь — о месте или обстановке; о человеке (I'm claustrophobic) — «страдающий клаустрофобией».
situation: You describe a tiny windowless room, a stuck lift or a small community where you feel trapped.

examples.text: The cabin on the night train was so [[claustrophobic]] that I spent most of the journey in the corridor.
Almost the whole film takes place in one small, dark flat, which gives it a [[claustrophobic]] feel.
Some patients find the scanner [[claustrophobic]], so the hospital offers music and a mirror to help them relax.

texts: Six of us shared a [[claustrophobic]] little office above the shop.
Everyone knew her business, and she found village life [[claustrophobic]].
The lift was tiny and [[claustrophobic]], so I took the stairs instead.

badCollocation.noteRu: После suffer from нужно существительное: suffer from claustrophobia. Claustrophobic — прилагательное: a claustrophobic lift.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Гнетущую, давящую атмосферу называют claustrophobic. Narrow, compact и small описывают размер предмета или помещения, а не атмосферу.

nuance.text: The room wasn't small, but with no windows it felt strangely [[claustrophobic]].
nuance.explanationRu: Cramped — тесный, где физически мало места. Claustrophobic — давящий, вызывающий желание выбраться. Комната здесь не маленькая, поэтому cramped противоречит смыслу.

fixIt.text: Being stuck in a broken lift for an hour was a truly [[claustrophobia]] experience.
fixIt.explanationRu: Перед существительным experience нужно прилагательное: a claustrophobic experience. Claustrophobia — существительное, название самой фобии.

wordFormation.text: People with [[claustrophobia]] often avoid lifts, tunnels and crowded trains.

reply.context: A colleague messages: "Shall we book the little meeting room on the fourth floor for tomorrow's workshop?"
options: Great idea — it's so claustrophobic that there'll be plenty of room for all twelve of us.
I'd rather not. With twelve of us and no windows, it'll feel pretty claustrophobic.
Please be informed that the aforementioned room is of a claustrophobic nature.
reply.explanationRu: Claustrophobic — тесный и давящий, это минус, а не «много места». Третий вариант звучит как официальное уведомление, а не ответ коллеге.

definitionEn: to keep holding on to a belief, hope or position you are afraid to lose
senseNote: Здесь — переносное значение (cling to hope, cling to power); в прямом смысле cling — крепко вцепиться в кого-то или что-то.
situation: Someone refuses to let go of power, an old belief or a fading hope, even when it seems unwise.

examples.text: Long after the divorce, he [[clung]] to the hope that she would one day come back.
Despite falling sales, the director is still [[clinging]] to a strategy she believes will work.
When life feels chaotic, many people [[cling]] to familiar routines that make them feel safe.

texts: Some politicians [[cling]] to power long after voters have lost faith in them.
It's natural to [[cling]] to hope when someone you love goes missing.
Older staff sometimes [[cling]] to methods they learned decades ago.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Цепляться за» — cling to (или cling on to), а не for: cling to power, cling to hope.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Держаться за власть вопреки всему — cling to power. Grab, grasp и catch значат «схватить» и с to в этом смысле не сочетаются.

nuance.text: Terrified of being alone, she [[clung]] to a relationship that was making her miserable.
nuance.explanationRu: Cling to — держаться за что-то из страха потерять, даже во вред себе. Stick to — придерживаться плана, правил или диеты; к отношениям, за которые держатся от страха, не подходит.

reverse.text: If you want to see results, you have to [[stick]] to the plan for at least a month.
reverse.explanationRu: Придерживаться плана, диеты или правил — stick to. Cling to звучит как отчаянная хватка за то, что ускользает, и для совета не подходит.

fixIt.text: Afraid of losing control, the company's ageing founder [[stuck]] to power until the board forced him out.
fixIt.explanationRu: Держаться за власть из страха её потерять — cling to power. Stick to — придерживаться плана или правил, с power не сочетается.

reply.context: A colleague writes: "The old booking system is slow and everyone hates it, but the boss won't let us replace it."
options: Kindly note that the manager is clinging to legacy infrastructure, as previously communicated.
Typical. He clings to every new app the moment it comes out.
Typical. He's clinging to it because he built it himself years ago.
reply.explanationRu: Cling to — упорно держаться за старое, а не хвататься за всё новое. Первый вариант — канцелярит, коллеге в чате так не пишут.

definitionEn: relating to the direct examination and treatment of patients
senseNote: Здесь — медицинское значение; clinical также значит «холодный, бесстрастный» (a clinical tone).
situation: Doctors and researchers talk about work with real patients, such as testing new drugs or diagnosing illness.

examples.text: The new drug will go through three years of [[clinical]] trials before it reaches pharmacies.
After ten years in the lab, she missed [[clinical]] work with real patients.
Her doctor explained that everyday sadness is very different from [[clinical]] depression.

texts: Student nurses spend months on [[clinical]] placements in busy hospitals.
The vaccine has now passed its final [[clinical]] trial.
The test result has little [[clinical]] significance, so don't worry.

badCollocation.noteRu: Больница при медицинском вузе — teaching hospital или university hospital; clinical hospital — калька с русского «клиническая больница».

collocationTask.explanationRu: Испытания лекарств на пациентах — clinical trials. Clinic — существительное (клиника), medicine trials так не говорят, а cynical значит «циничный».

nuance.text: Before approval, every new treatment must pass strict [[clinical]] tests on patients.
nuance.explanationRu: Clinical — связанный с обследованием и лечением пациентов: clinical tests, clinical trials. Medicinal — целебный, лечебный: medicinal herbs, medicinal properties.

reverse.text: Many common garden plants have [[medicinal]] properties.
reverse.explanationRu: Целебные свойства растений — medicinal properties. Clinical относится к работе врачей с пациентами, а не к свойствам трав.

fixIt.text: Before a new medicine is approved, it must pass several stages of [[clinic]] testing.
fixIt.explanationRu: Перед существительным testing нужно прилагательное: clinical testing. Clinic — существительное: поликлиника или частная клиника.

wordFormation.text: The hospital is known for combining research with excellent [[clinical]] care.

reply.context: A friend who works as a nurse tells you: "I'm thinking of leaving the ward for an office job in hospital management."
options: Really? Won't you miss the clinical side — actually looking after patients?
Really? Won't you miss the clinical side — all the budgets and meetings?
Kindly elaborate on the rationale for your clinical-to-administrative transition.
reply.explanationRu: Clinical — связанный с лечением пациентов, а не с бюджетами и совещаниями. Третий вариант звучит как анкета отдела кадров, а не разговор с другом.

definitionEn: a feeling that a painful experience has truly ended, so you can move on
senseNote: Здесь — эмоциональное значение (need closure); базовое значение — закрытие предприятия или дороги (factory closure, road closure).
situation: After a breakup, a loss or a long court case, someone finally feels able to put it behind them.

examples.text: Clearing out her late mother's flat was painful, but it gave her some [[closure]].
Breaking up by text gave neither of them [[closure]], so they finally met for coffee.
The official apology gave the victims' families the sense of [[closure]] they had waited decades for.

texts: After the divorce, I just wanted [[closure]], not revenge.
Therapy helped him find [[closure]] after his brother's death.
The final episode gave fans the [[closure]] they had hoped for.

badCollocation.noteRu: Closure не «делают»: говорят get, find или need closure, а также bring someone closure.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Чувство, что тяжёлая история позади, — a sense of closure. End, finish и closing просто значат «конец» и в этом выражении не используются.

nuance.text: Being fired without any explanation left him angry, and he never really got [[closure]].
nuance.explanationRu: Closure — внутреннее ощущение, что тяжёлая история закончилась и можно жить дальше. Conclusion — вывод или заключительная часть доклада; о чувствах так не говорят.

reverse.text: In the [[conclusion]], the authors suggest three ways to reduce costs.
reverse.explanationRu: Заключительная часть текста — conclusion. Closure — о внутреннем чувстве завершённости у человека, а не о разделе отчёта.

fixIt.text: Honestly, I just want to see him once more, say goodbye and get some [[completeness]].
fixIt.explanationRu: Эмоциональная «завершённость» — closure: get some closure. Completeness — полнота (данных, списка), о чувствах после расставания так не говорят.

wordFormation.text: Some people write letters they never send, just to get a little [[closure]].

reply.context: A friend texts: "My ex wants to meet up and talk things through. Should I go?"
options: Go! Closure is great — you two might even get back together.
Please be advised that closure may be obtained by attending the meeting.
Only if you want closure. If you're secretly hoping to get back together, maybe don't.
reply.explanationRu: Closure — ощущение, что история закончена и её можно отпустить, а не шанс всё вернуть. Второй вариант звучит как официальное письмо, а не ответ другу.

definitionEn: a small group of similar things or people that are close together
situation: You describe several similar things, like houses, stars or cases of an illness, grouped closely together.

examples.text: A small [[cluster]] of white houses sits on the hillside above the harbour.
Doctors noticed an unusual [[cluster]] of flu cases among staff at one office.
The old docks now host a [[cluster]] of tech start-ups and design studios.

texts: On a clear night you can see a bright [[cluster]] of stars.
Tiny white flowers grow in a dense [[cluster]] at the end of each stem.
The hotel is a [[cluster]] of wooden cabins beside the lake.

badCollocation.noteRu: Большое «скопление людей» — a crowd. Cluster — небольшая группка людей или предметов, стоящих рядом.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Звёздное скопление — a cluster of stars. Flock говорят о птицах и овцах, pack — о волках или картах, pile — о куче вещей.

nuance.text: Scientists have identified a [[cluster]] of genes linked to the disease.
nuance.explanationRu: Cluster — нейтральное, в том числе научное слово для группы похожих объектов рядом. Bunch — разговорное («пучок», «куча»), в научном тексте звучит небрежно.

reverse.text: He came home with a [[bunch]] of flowers from the market.
reverse.explanationRu: Букет или связка, которую держат в руках (цветов, ключей), — a bunch. Cluster — группа предметов, которые растут или стоят рядом.

fixIt.text: Astronomers have discovered a new [[accumulation]] of young stars in our galaxy.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Скопление» звёзд, домов или случаев болезни — cluster. Accumulation — постепенное накопление (пыли, долгов, опыта), а не группа объектов рядом.

rewrite.original: Several small houses stood close together near the river.
rewrite.frame: A small ____ stood near the river.
rewrite.explanationRu: Несколько домов, стоящих рядом, — a cluster of houses.

definitionEn: a group of parties or organisations that join together for a shared aim
situation: Several political parties or groups agree to work together, often to form a government or fight for a cause.

examples.text: Since no party won a majority, three of them formed a [[coalition]] to run the country.
A [[coalition]] of charities and local businesses is campaigning to save the town library.
The two countries joined an international [[coalition]] to fight plastic pollution in the oceans.

texts: The [[coalition]] collapsed after the two parties disagreed over taxes.
Environmental groups have joined the [[coalition]] against the new airport.
Critics say the ruling [[coalition]] has no clear plan for the economy.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Коалиция из двух партий» — a coalition of two parties; предлог from здесь не подходит.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Коалицию создают глаголом form (а также build или join). Make, do и take с coalition не сочетаются.

nuance.text: After weeks of talks, the new [[coalition]] government was finally sworn in.
nuance.explanationRu: Правительство из нескольких партий — coalition government, это устойчивое сочетание. Alliance — союз, чаще стран или компаний и надолго; alliance government не говорят.

reverse.text: Several airlines have joined an [[alliance]] so that passengers can collect points with any of them.
reverse.explanationRu: Долгосрочный союз компаний или стран — alliance (airline alliance). Coalition — чаще временное объединение партий или групп ради конкретной цели.

fixIt.text: Most experts expect a [[coalitional]] government after Sunday's election.
fixIt.explanationRu: Правительство из нескольких партий — coalition government: существительное coalition работает как определение. Форма coalitional почти не используется.

reply.context: In a politics seminar, the tutor asks: "What usually happens when no party wins a majority?"
options: The biggest party forms a coalition on its own and simply governs alone.
Well, they just kind of coalition up, or whatever.
Often two or more parties form a coalition and agree to share power.
reply.explanationRu: Coalition — союз нескольких партий: в одиночку коалицию не создают. Второй ответ слишком небрежный для семинара, и coalition не бывает глаголом.

rewrite.original: After the election, two parties agreed to govern the country together.
rewrite.frame: After the election, two parties formed ____.
rewrite.explanationRu: Совместное правление нескольких партий — a coalition (government).

definitionEn: on, near or connected with the land beside the sea
senseNote: У слова одно значение; здесь оно показано в типичных для C1 сочетаниях (coastal erosion, coastal waters).
situation: You talk about towns, roads, waters or wildlife on the land right next to the sea.

examples.text: Rising sea levels are putting many [[coastal]] communities at risk of flooding.
We spent the weekend walking a [[coastal]] path with amazing views of the cliffs.
Fishing and tourism are the main sources of income in this [[coastal]] region.

texts: Winter storms have caused serious [[coastal]] erosion in the east.
Dolphins are often spotted in these [[coastal]] waters in summer.
The old [[coastal]] road winds past fishing villages and quiet beaches.

badCollocation.noteRu: Береговая охрана — the coastguard (или coast guard), без -al. Coastal значит «прибрежный»: coastal waters, coastal towns.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Прибрежные воды — coastal waters. Seaside говорят о курортах и отдыхе (a seaside town), beachy — разговорное «пляжный», coasting — от глагола «катиться по инерции».

nuance.text: Engineers are building new [[coastal]] defences to protect the town from storms.
nuance.explanationRu: Coastal — нейтральное, географическое «прибрежный»: coastal defences, coastal erosion. Seaside связано с отдыхом у моря (a seaside holiday, a seaside town) и к защитным сооружениям не подходит.

fixIt.text: House prices in [[marine]] towns have risen sharply since remote working became common.
fixIt.explanationRu: Города на побережье — coastal towns. Marine — «морской» в биологическом смысле: marine life, marine biology.

wordFormation.text: The ferry stops at every small [[coastal]] village along the way.

reply.context: A friend asks: "Where should we go for a quiet weekend away in October?"
options: I would recommend a coastal locality offering adequate accommodation facilities.
How about that little coastal town we drove through? Long walks, fresh fish, no crowds.
How about a coastal village high in the mountains, far from the sea?
reply.explanationRu: Coastal — у моря, поэтому «в горах, далеко от моря» — противоречие. Первый ответ звучит как отчёт турагентства, а не совет другу.

definitionEn: connected with thinking, learning, remembering and understanding
situation: Psychologists and doctors describe mental abilities such as memory, attention and problem-solving, and how they change with age.

examples.text: Regular exercise may help to slow [[cognitive]] decline in older adults.
Puzzles and board games support young children's [[cognitive]] development in a playful way.
Constant notifications increase our [[cognitive]] load and make it harder to concentrate.

texts: Lack of sleep affects your [[cognitive]] performance the next day.
Brain-training apps claim to boost your [[cognitive]] abilities in minutes a day.
The patient showed no signs of [[cognitive]] impairment after the fall.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Познавательный» фильм или передача — educational или informative. Cognitive — научный термин о мышлении: cognitive skills, cognitive decline.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Ухудшение памяти и мышления — cognitive decline. Mind и thinking — существительные и в этой роли не используются, а intelligent — «умный» о человеке.

nuance.text: She studied [[cognitive]] science, which combines psychology, linguistics and computing.
nuance.explanationRu: Cognitive — научный термин о процессах мышления, отсюда название дисциплины cognitive science. Mental — общее «психический, умственный»: mental health, mental illness.

reverse.text: Talking openly about [[mental]] health at work is becoming more common.
reverse.explanationRu: Психическое здоровье — mental health. Cognitive относится только к мышлению и памяти, а не к эмоциональному состоянию человека.

fixIt.text: Memory, attention and reasoning are all [[psychic]] abilities that can be trained.
fixIt.explanationRu: Psychic — «экстрасенсорный» (psychic powers). Память, внимание и логика — cognitive abilities, то есть познавательные способности.

wordFormation.text: Researchers are studying how poor sleep affects [[cognition]] in teenagers.

reply.context: At an interview for a job at a nursery, you're asked: "Why do you think play matters so much for small children?"
options: Play builds cognitive skills like memory and problem-solving, and social skills too.
Play is mostly cognitive — it's about running around and burning off energy.
Play is, like, super cognitive and stuff, you know?
reply.explanationRu: Cognitive — связанный с мышлением и памятью, а не с беготнёй и физической энергией. Третий ответ слишком разговорный и пустой для собеседования.

definitionEn: to happen at the same time as something else
senseNote: Здесь — «совпадать по времени»; о мнениях или интересах (our views coincide) — «совпадать, сходиться».
situation: Two events happen on the same day or at the same moment, by chance or because someone planned it.

examples.text: The strike was timed to [[coincide]] with the start of the tourist season.
My holiday [[coincides]] with the conference, so I'm afraid I can't give a talk.
The opening of the new museum [[coincided]] with the city's 800th anniversary.

texts: We planned the product launch to [[coincide]] with the trade fair.
It's rare for our days off to [[coincide]], so we hardly see each other.
The two exams [[coincide]], so I'll have to choose one.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Совпадать по времени» — просто coincide (with something); by time или in time добавлять не нужно.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Приурочить событие к другому — time something to coincide with. Match — подходить по виду, fit — по размеру, meet — встречаться; здесь они не подходят.

nuance.text: The shop's big sale was planned to [[coincide]] with payday.
nuance.explanationRu: Coincide — просто совпадать по времени, часто специально. Clash — неудачно совпасть и мешать друг другу; нарочно планировать такое странно.

fixIt.text: Our holiday dates [[matched]] with the carnival, so every hotel in town was full.
fixIt.explanationRu: Совпасть по времени — coincide with. Match значит «соответствовать, подходить» (цвета, данные) и о событиях в таком значении не используется.

wordFormation.text: By pure [[coincidence]], my new manager grew up on the same street as me.

reply.context: Your manager emails: "Could you run the training session on the 14th?"
options: Sure — it coincides perfectly, because I'm on holiday that week.
I'd love to, but it coincides with a client visit. Would the 15th work?
Negative. A coincidence of engagements renders me unavailable.
reply.explanationRu: Coincide — совпадать по времени, поэтому «идеально совпадает, ведь я в отпуске» звучит нелепо. Третий ответ слишком резкий и канцелярский для письма руководителю.

rewrite.original: The concert and the football final are on the same evening.

definitionEn: to work together with other people to create or achieve something
senseNote: Здесь — «сотрудничать»; collaborate with the enemy — «сотрудничать с врагом» (неодобрительно).
situation: People from different teams, companies or countries work together on a shared project, such as a study or an album.

examples.text: Researchers from six countries [[collaborated]] on the study, sharing their data online.
The two authors are [[collaborating]] on a novel, writing alternate chapters.
If we [[collaborate]] with the marketing team from the start, the launch will go much more smoothly.

texts: Our two departments rarely [[collaborate]], which causes a lot of confusion.
Artists and scientists will [[collaborate]] on an exhibition about climate.
Students are encouraged to [[collaborate]] rather than compete for grades.

badCollocation.noteRu: Над проектом работают вместе с предлогом: collaborate on a project; с людьми — collaborate with someone.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Тесно работать с другой командой — collaborate closely with. Combine — соединять вещи, join — присоединяться, gather — собираться; с closely with они не сочетаются.

nuance.text: The two directors [[collaborated]] on the screenplay for almost three years.
nuance.explanationRu: Collaborate — вместе создавать что-то (книгу, фильм, исследование). Cooperate — содействовать, выполнять просьбы, не мешать; о совместной работе над сценарием звучит слабее.

reverse.text: The suspect refused to [[cooperate]] with the police.
reverse.explanationRu: Выполнять требования полиции, не мешать следствию — cooperate. Collaborate — совместно что-то создавать, к допросу не подходит.

fixIt.text: For her new album, she [[contributed]] with a young jazz pianist from New Orleans.
fixIt.explanationRu: Работать вместе с кем-то — collaborate with someone. Contribute — вносить вклад (contribute to something), with после него в этом смысле не ставят.

wordFormation.text: The course takes a [[collaborative]] approach, with students working in small teams.

reply.context: A colleague from another department messages: "We're both working on customer surveys at the moment. Shall we join forces?"
options: Great idea! Let's collaborate and share what we've found so far.
Great idea! Let's collaborate, but work separately and not share anything.
Your proposal to collaborate is hereby accepted in full.
reply.explanationRu: Collaborate — работать вместе, поэтому «сотрудничать, ничего не показывая друг другу» — противоречие. Третий ответ звучит как официальный приказ, а не ответ коллеге.
